decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY that fully captures the necessary effect: every remaining letter must belong to the Hero V's proprietary architectural alphabet and must not appear adapted from an existing typeface.

The second V already remains part of the proprietary V system and is derived from the approved Hero V geometry. Message 154 separately refines its height and visual role in an existing same-message MODIFY, while the source architectural-language clarification adds no further necessary state change.

The accent's current state already requires literal derivation from the approved Hero V terminal with exact geometry and alignment. The broader architectural-language role does not alter those accent-specific rules.

The source explicitly says the Hero V governs more than stroke weight and termination details, but it does not change the existing shared-terminal geometry or treatment. The broader effect belongs to the proprietary letterform Requirement.
The source clarification governs construction of the remaining proprietary letterforms, not the composition Requirement's kerning, rhythm, case treatment, or established vertical hierarchy.

The brand-expression state already describes the desired architectural and proprietary character. Message 154 supplies a concrete letter-construction rule rather than changing the broader emotional positioning or brand-expression attributes.
The Hero V's expanded architectural-language role does not change the deferred champagne-metal material, its qualities, or the rule that geometry must be resolved before material treatment.
The source does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram. It only clarifies how the Hero V governs the wordmark's letterform language.
